title: 基礎生物学Ⅱ
subtitle: Basic Biology II
keywords: Organelle 2.Energy Metabolism 3.Reproduction and Heredity 4.Homeostasis 5.Biomimetics and AI
educationalGoal: Based on knowledge acquired in Basic Biology 1, this course cultivates further understanding of common features and diversity of life. This objective is achieved by learning and discussing on the topics including (1) cell structure and genetics behind common biological functions, (2) variation in respiratory substrates and photosynthetic pathways underlying organisms diversity, and (3) industrial application of biological structures and functions.
advice: We will cover the following materials: 1. Structure and function of organelle, 2. Energy metabolism, 3. Regulation of gene expression, 4. Reproduction and heredity, 5. Signal transduction in disease, 6. Material cycles in ecosystem, and 7. Human uses of biology. This course is designed to be understandable even to the students who have not taken the biology course in high school. However, students are highly recommended to go through, in advance, the contents of high school biology. Students should pay attention to the teacher’s instructions in the class since the schedule may change depending on the class progresses. Students should attend all classes; otherwise, the handouts may not be received. Students are expected to check for messages/materials on the KIT Inside website before each class.
books: Textbooks:Daigakusei no tameno kangaete manabu Kisoseibutsugaku (Kyoritsu Shuppan) Reference books:Seibutsugaku jiten (Iwanami Shoten) Reserved books:None
requiredKnowledge: Basic knowledge of biology. Basic computer skills. Students are requested to prepare for and review each class.

activityGoals.body: Ability to explain structures and functions of cell organelle
Ability to explain biological energy consumption
Ability to explain features of sexual and asexual reproduction
Ability to explain chromosomal basis of inheritance
Ability to explain the role of hormones in homeostasis
Ability to design and conduct literature research and oral presentation on biofunctions/biomimetics

achievementLevels.ideal: (1) Fully understand the structure-function relationship of cell organelle. (2) Fully understand the mechanism of biological energy consumption. (3) Fully understand advantage, disadvantage and the mechanism of sexual and asexual reproduction. (4) Fully understand the chromosomal basis of inheritance. (5) Fully understand the role of hormones in homeostasis and health. (6) Present a novel idea for application of biofunctions and biomimetics.
achievementLevels.standard: (1) Explain structures and functions of cell organelle. (2) Explain biological energy consumption. (3) Explain features of sexual and asexual reproduction. (4) Explain the chromosomal basis of inheritance. (5) Explain significance of hormones in homeostasis. (6) Present application examples of biofunctions and biomimetics.

lessons.content: Course introduction Structure and function of cell organelle
Building blocks of life: Carbohydrates and lipids Methods of protein detection
Energy and metabolism: regulatory mechanism of enzymatic reaction, unconventional photosynthesis, and nitrogen assimilation
lessons.assignments: Read pages 42-44 and 47-50 of the textbook.

lessons.content: Energy and metabolism: catabolism of proteins and lipids, uses of ATP, and passive and active transport
Gene and heredity: regulation of gene expression, and types of mutation
lessons.assignments: Read pages 75 and 81-86 of the textbook.

lessons.content: Midterm review of classes Group meeting for literature research on application of biofunctions
lessons.assignments: Review contents of Classes 1-5. Conduct literature research.

lessons.content: Gene and heredity: gametogenesis, and ways of reproduction
Gene and heredity: Mendel's law of independent assortment, and sex chromosome inheritance
Homeostasis and immunity: hormones for homeostasis
Homeostasis and immunity: immunity in disease
Biofunctions and biodiversity: material cycles and energy flows in ecosystems, and human uses of biology
lessons.assignments: Read pages 169-176 and 196-197 of the textbook.

lessons.content: Term-end review of classes Finalization of literature research
lessons.assignments: Review contents of Classes 1-11. Finalize literature research.

lessons.content: Biofunctions and biodiversity: environmental adaptation of organisms Progress discussion on literature research
lessons.operation: Lecture and Q&A Group work Self-check

lessons.content: Group presentation of literature research on application of biofunctions
